html:
John Hanning Speke was a British explorer who identified Lake Victoria as the source of the White Nile, reaching its southern shore in 1858 and the outflow at Ripon Falls, near Jinja in Uganda, on 28 July 1862.

He first travelled with Richard Burton, who doubted his claim. On his second journey he stayed at the court of Muteesa I before finding where the Nile leaves the lake.

His claim was disputed in Britain, and he died of a gunshot wound while hunting in 1864, a day before a planned debate with Burton. Later explorers, among them Stanley, confirmed he was right. The falls were later drowned by the Owen Falls Dam.
